headline.purpose: Prompts, feedback outcomes, and dive-log titles.

title.purpose: Short mode names and prominent operational labels.

label.purpose: Uppercase HUD data, controls, round state, and compact metadata.

shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: Ambient separation for launch control and the final dive log.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: Compact standalone controls such as audio.

shadows.name: spine-separation
shadows.purpose: Lateral depth between the desktop telemetry spine and the live stage.

shadows.name: surface-glow
shadows.purpose: Environmental light near the ocean surface; not a container shadow.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Buttons, pack cards, borders, and short hover changes.

motion.name: panel-arrival
motion.purpose: Prompt, feedback, and dive-log entrance; feedback uses the score-slam keyframes.

motion.name: title-flicker
motion.purpose: Sparse broadcast flicker on the OMNIQUIZ launch wordmark.

motion.name: ocean-descent

components.name: Begin Descent Button
components.description: The full-width coral launch action that begins or retries a mission.
components.css: .ds-begin-button { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; width: min(100%, 420px); min-height: 62px; padding: 0.8rem 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--coral, #ff667f); border-bottom-width: 5px; border-radius: 0; background: #6e2638; color: var(--paper, #edf7f7); font-family: var(--pixel, "Pixelify Sans Variable", "Pixelify Sans", monospace); font-size: 0.8rem; letter-spacing: 0.16em; transition: background 140ms ease-out, color 140ms ease-out, transform 140ms ease-out; } .ds-begin-button b { font: inherit; } .ds-descent-mark { width: 9px; height: 9px; border-right: 2px solid currentColor; border-bottom: 2px solid currentColor; transform: rotate(45deg) translateY(-2px); } .ds-begin-button:hover { background: var(--coral, #ff667f); color: #17070d; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-begin-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--paper, #edf7f7); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-begin-button:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Dive Submit Button

narrative.overview:
OMNIQUIZ presents a trivia run as a live 16-bit dive operation. A cold, detailed ocean raster owns the world while coral and cyan telemetry, scanlines, a depth ruler, and instrument panels turn every answer into mission data rather than generic quiz chrome.

The experience tells one continuous operational story: launch control hands off to a dominant live prompt feed, feedback slams the score and depth into view, and the run resolves as a compact dive log. The density is cinematic but controlled; the current prompt remains the only dominant reading surface while telemetry stays peripheral and explicit.
keyCharacteristics: Project-owned pixel-ocean and hull rasters, never stock-photo scenery or generic sci-fi framing.
A desktop vertical telemetry spine beside one dominant live stage; a top instrument dock on mobile.
One self-hosted variable bitmap family across display, prompts, controls, and metadata.
Cold navy material with cyan navigation, coral action, gold rarity, and restrained green pack accents.
Depth-driven environmental change, deliberate score and urgency motion, and a complete reduced-motion fallback.

rules.name: The Three-Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan navigates and reports depth, coral acts and scores, and gold marks rarity; keep those meanings stable.

rules.name: The Dark-Water Rule
rules.body: Large surfaces remain near-black navy so Phosphor Paper and the mission signals carry the hierarchy.

rules.name: The One-Broadcast Voice Rule
rules.body: Keep display, prompts, controls, and telemetry in Pixelify Sans; hierarchy comes from the variable weight axis and spacing, not a second family.

rules.name: The Tracking Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Wide uppercase tracking belongs to short operational labels; prompts and explanatory sentences stay tightly tracked.

rules.name: The Telemetry Spine Rule
rules.body: On desktop, preserve a narrow vertical instrument spine and give the remaining viewport to one framed live stage; on mobile, move the same data into the top dock.

rules.name: The One Live Feed Rule
rules.body: Prompt or feedback is the sole dominant panel; score, depth, timing, navigation, and progress remain instrumentation around it.

rules.name: The Raster Owns the World Rule
rules.body: The mission panorama and both hull-frame assets are first-class material; preserve their pixel rendering and do not replace them with stock imagery, blur glass, or generic gradient frames.

rules.name: The Glow Means Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan and coral glow belongs to active progress, the critical timer, or environmental light; resting containers do not all glow.

rules.name: The Circle Is a Gauge Rule
rules.body: Use the full-circle token for measured instrumentation, not for general actions, cards, chips, or navigation.

dos: Do keep the owned panorama and hull rasters pixel-sharp and structurally central.
Do preserve the desktop spine/live-stage split and the mobile top-dock transformation at 700px.
Do keep prompts high-contrast and singular while telemetry stays peripheral.
Do use cyan for navigation/depth, coral for action/score/urgency, and gold for rarity.
Do make controls keyboard reachable, at least 44px tall, safe-area aware, and operable with reduced motion.
Do let score and depth visibly alter the environment as well as the numbers.
donts: Don't replace the ROV world with stock ocean photography, smooth vector gradients, or generic sci-fi glass panels.
Don't introduce pills, softened SaaS cards, blur-heavy glassmorphism, or rounded navigation.
Don't use coral, cyan, gold, and green as interchangeable decoration.
Don't add a proportional display or body family; the shipped system uses one Pixelify Sans variable voice.
Don't stretch the prompt beyond 620px or the answer hull beyond 690px on desktop.
Don't rely on motion alone to communicate timer urgency, progress, feedback, score, or depth.
